item.title: Middle East conflict causes a fluoride shortage for US drinking water
item.summary: Some U.S. water systems are cutting back on fluoride because of a key chemical is in short supply. Israel is one of its main producers.

item.title: Jury finds that Live Nation acted as a monopoly and overcharged ticket buyers
item.summary: An antitrust suit alleged that the company unfairly controlled too much of the live music industry at the expense of venues, artists and fans. The decision could reshape the industry.

item.title: Whiting Foundation names its 10 emerging authors of 2026
item.summary: The annual Whiting Award for Emerging Writers comes with $50,000 to support each winner's work. It's one of the largest prizes granted to promising new authors.

item.title: Popes have spoken out on politics before. But with Trump and Pope Leo it's different
item.summary: President Trump's attacks on Pope Leo are unprecedented, religious experts told NPR. Here's how the situation differs from other popes' political critiques.

item.title: [PENDING_TRANSLATION] Tune in to a mini-concert with Tedeschi Trucks Band
item.summary: The 12-piece outfit performs music from their latest album, Future Soul.

item.title: Once again, Trump threatens to fire Fed Chair Jerome Powell
item.summary: President Trump once again threatened to fire Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell and doubled down on a discredited probe of the central bank.

item.title: Greetings from Nairobi, where taking a matatu is no ordinary bus ride
item.summary: The moment you board, the music grabs you. These privately owned, brightly painted minibuses are moving canvases, mobile sound systems — rolling declarations of what young Nairobi finds cool.

item.title: Exploring the green side of Rio de Janeiro: a vast urban rain forest
item.summary: Rio de Janeiro in Brazil is home to the world's largest urban rain forest. Woven among the city's bustling neighborhoods are soaring tree canopies, waterfalls, and miles of hiking trails.

item.title: Actor Amanda Peet says she's 'cancer-free and extremely lucky'
item.summary: Peet is always waiting for the other shoe to drop. Except last year there seemed to be three different shoes, as she faced her parents' deaths and a breast cancer diagnosis.

item.title: Visionary NPR leader Kevin Klose, who led network to new heights, has died
item.summary: Klose led NPR for a decade starting in 1998, a period of incredible growth for the public media network.
